Glossary

    Trigonometry

    Words: 1326

    The ratios of the sides of a right triangle, which depend only on the angle, let loose around a circle: this is how an angle becomes any number, and sine and cosine become functions.

    Main idea of the page #

    Trigonometry grew out of the similarity of triangles (block 10): in similar right triangles the ratios of the sides are equal, so they depend only on the angle. The unit circle turns these ratios into the coordinates of a point: Sine and cosineThe ordinate and the abscissa of the point of the unit circle that corresponds to the angle α.To the glossary . Almost all the formulas come from here: the basic identity is Pythagoras' theoremIn a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the legs.To the glossary on the circle, the reduction formulas are symmetries of the circle. The block can describe what repeats; the price for it is the infinite series of roots.

    Step 0 · Hook

    1 · Is the sine of a sum the sum of the sines? #

    The habit of expanding brackets suggests: sin(α+β)=sinα+sinβ\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha + \sin\beta. Let us check at α=β=30∘\alpha = \beta = 30^\circ: on the left sin60∘≈0.87\sin 60^\circ \approx 0.87, on the right 0.5+0.5=10.5 + 0.5 = 1. Sine is not a factor but a function, and the distributive law does not apply to it.

    Step 1 · Concept

    2 · The radian and the unit circle #

    • A RadianThe angle that stands on an arc as long as the radius.To the glossary is the angle that stands on an arc as long as the radius. A full circle is 2π2\pi radians, so 180∘=π180^\circ = \pi.
    • The Unit circleThe circle of radius 1 centred at the origin, on which angles are measured off.To the glossary is the circle of radius 1 centred at the origin. The angle α is measured from the positive direction of the Ox axis anticlockwise.
    • cosα\cos\alpha is the AbscissaThe first coordinate of a point: its projection on the Ox axis.To the glossary of the point of the circle, sinα\sin\alpha is the ordinate, tanα=sinαcosα\tan\alpha = \frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}.
    • After a full turn the point comes back: sine and cosine are Periodic functionA function whose values repeat after a constant step, the period.To the glossary with period 2π2\pi.
    Step 2 · Law

    3 · Laws of trigonometry #

    Basic trigonometric identity

    sin2α+cos2α=1\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1

    Sine and cosine of a sum

    sin(α±β)=sinαcosβ±cosαsinβ\sin(\alpha \pm \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta \pm \cos\alpha\sin\beta
    cos(α±β)=cosαcosβ∓sinαsinβ\cos(\alpha \pm \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta \mp \sin\alpha\sin\beta

    Double angle

    sin2α=2sinαcosα,cos2α=cos2α−sin2α=1−2sin2α\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha,\qquad \cos 2\alpha = \cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^2\alpha

    Reduction formulas

    For the angles π±α\pi \pm \alpha, 2π±α2\pi \pm \alpha the name of the function stays, for π2±α\frac{\pi}{2} \pm \alpha, 3π2±α\frac{3\pi}{2} \pm \alpha it changes (sine to cosine and back). The sign is the one the original function has in the quadrant where the angle landed.

    The simplest equations

    sinx=a: x=(−1)karcsina+πk;cosx=a: x=±arccosa+2πk\sin x = a:\ x = (-1)^k \arcsin a + \pi k;\qquad \cos x = a:\ x = \pm\arccos a + 2\pi k

    where k is any integer, and |a|≤1|a| \leq 1.

    Step 3 · Why it is so

    4 · All of this is the circle #

    The identity. The point (cosα; sinα)(\cos\alpha;\ \sin\alpha) lies on the circle of radius 1, that is, its distance to the centre is 1. By Pythagoras' theorem this is exactly cos2α+sin2α=1\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha = 1.

    Figure 26. Sine and cosine are the coordinates of a point of the unit circle; the identity is Pythagoras' theorem.

    Reduction formulas. The angles α and π−α\pi - \alpha are symmetric about the Oy axis: the ordinates are equal, the abscissas are opposite. Hence sin(π−α)=sinα\sin(\pi - \alpha) = \sin\alpha, cos(π−α)=−cosα\cos(\pi - \alpha) = -\cos\alpha. The other formulas are other symmetries of the circle.

    Figure 27. A reduction formula as a symmetry of the circle: sin(π − α) = sin α.

    The double angle is the sum formula with β=α\beta = \alpha. And 1−2sin2α1 - 2\sin^2\alpha is obtained by the substitution cos2α=1−sin2α\cos^2\alpha = 1 - \sin^2\alpha from the identity.

    Series of roots. The equation sinx=a\sin x = a on the circle is the horizontal line y=ay = a. It crosses the circle at two points (symmetric about Oy), and each of them repeats after a full turn.

    Figure 28. sin x = 1/2: two points on one turn, then repetition every 2π.

    Step 4 · Limits

    5 · Where the laws break #

    Sine and cosine do not leave [−1; 1]. The OrdinateThe second coordinate of a point: its projection on the Oy axis.To the glossary of a point of a circle of radius 1 cannot be 1.5. So sinx=1.5\sin x = 1.5 has no solutions, and the record arcsin1.5\arcsin 1.5 makes no sense.

    The tangent does not exist where the cosine is zero: at x=π2+πkx = \frac{\pi}{2} + \pi k.

    The identity gives the absolute value, the sign gives the quadrant. From cosα=0.6\cos\alpha = 0.6 it follows that sinα=±0.8\sin\alpha = \pm 0.8; which sign is decided by the quadrant in which the angle lies.

    Step 5 · Practice

    6 · Tasks in the NMT format #

    One answer out of five · 1 point

    It is known that cosα=0.6\cos\alpha = 0.6 and α is an acute angle. Find sinα\sin\alpha.

    Law: the basic identity.

    sin2α=1−0.36=0.64\sin^2\alpha = 1 - 0.36 = 0.64, the angle is acute, so sinα=0.8\sin\alpha = 0.8. 0.4 is the blind «1 − 0.6», 0.64 is a forgotten root.

    Short answer · 2 points

    Calculate sin217∘+cos217∘+tan45∘\sin^2 17^\circ + \cos^2 17^\circ + \tan 45^\circ.

    Law: the basic identity.

    The first two terms give 1 at any angle, tan45∘=1\tan 45^\circ = 1. In all 2. The angle 17° is bait: no table is needed for it.

    One answer out of five · 1 point

    Calculate sin150∘\sin 150^\circ.

    Law: reduction formulas.

    sin(180∘−30∘)=sin30∘=12\sin(180^\circ - 30^\circ) = \sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}. In the second quadrant sine is positive, so the minus in option A is a sign mistake.

    Matching · 3 points

    Match each expression (1-3) with the one identically equal to it (A-E).

    A · cos²α   B · sin 2α   C · cos 2α   D · tan α   E · 1

    Laws: double angle, the basic identity.

    Two double-angle formulas and the identity, read from right to left.
    Step 6 · Reverse move

    7 · Name the law yourself #

    Short answer · 2 points

    How many roots does the equation sinx=12\sin x = \frac{1}{2} have on the interval

    0; 2π0;\ 2\pi
    ?

    Law: the simplest equations and the circle.

    The line y=12y = \frac{1}{2} crosses the circle at two points: π6\frac{\pi}{6} and 5π6\frac{5\pi}{6}. One turn gives two roots.

    Short answer · 2 points

    Find cos2α\cos 2\alpha if sinα=0.3\sin\alpha = 0.3.

    Law: the double angle in the form through the sine.

    1−2·0.09=0.821 - 2 \cdot 0.09 = 0.82. There is no need to find the cosine, and the sign of the angle does not matter: the sine is squared.

    8 · Find the mistake in someone else's solution #

    Sofia solves 2sinx=32\sin x = 3: «sinx=1.5\sin x = 1.5, so x=(−1)karcsin1.5+πkx = (-1)^k \arcsin 1.5 + \pi k».

    Where is the mistake?

    Sine is never greater than 1 (the first limit). The equation has no solutions, and the series formula applies only when |a|≤1|a| \leq 1.

    What you have after this page #

    The unit circle instead of tables. The identity is Pythagoras on the circle, the reduction formulas are symmetries of the circle, the series of roots are repetition after a full turn. The circle can be drawn on scrap paper in ten seconds, and it will answer most of the questions of the block.

    Frequency on this site, not in the NMT: this page has 6 trainer tasks, and they lean on these laws: Basic trigonometric identity - 3, Double angle - 2, Reduction formulas - 1, The simplest equations - 1. In real NMT papers of 2024-2026 this block is needed in 6 tasks out of 132: Reduction formulas - 5, The simplest equations - 1.
